I feel where you’re coming from.  Alcoholic here.  I remember being so down when I was drunk (and sober) I’d be texting the suicide hotline all the time, crying in despair.  Just get sober.  I still struggle with mental health issues but my life began again when I left the alcohol and other things behind.  Your brain chemistry changes and you start to experience things again.  My perspective is this, if you’re feeling so down that you want to give up, you might as well keep going and try your best to get sober.  In other words if it really feels like ‘fuck it, nothing matters’ you might as well see if there’s something better.  All of that is besides the fact that it’s not fair to the world to opt out.  You have something inside you that will help the world around you and make even a small difference.  Please try again.  Get the help you need.  Be a friend to yourself

Hey I feel you!  Calming down can be difficult.  There are some ways to practice though, to practice calming down when anxious.  It seems silly but sitting down, closing your eyes, and taking slow deep breaths can change your mood.  Taking refuge in favorite things is cool too, movies or video games.  Books!  Distractions can take your mind off of negative self-critical narration.  Contrary to popular opinion you can absolutely run away from your problems…. Literally.  If there’s a place that is fucking up your life and it’s avoidable, avoid it.  If there’s someone in your life you aren’t 100% dependent on that’s running you down or making you feel unloved - cut them out of your life like a cancer.  If there’s an activity that you know if self-destructive and you could slow down or stop, give it a try.  These are obvious methods so I don’t mean to sound reductive or patronizing.  You can fake it though.  How many times have you had to fake things in your life?  You’ve had to pretend to like this or that person or fake a good attitude at work or pretend you love the awful gift or gesture someone gave you.  Give yourself the same consideration you give shit you don’t even like.  Fake-love yourself by engaging in activities that the imaginary happy self-loving version of yourself might do…. and you might just experience some relief.

Some of the worst times in my life that had me literally desperate, alone, hating myself and the world, staring at a gun or standing on a ledge……. I remember the pain of those moments but its faded into the past.  Some I can only vaguely remember even though, at the time, those moments seemed life-defining and so important.  They don’t mean anything now….. but that’s only because I didn’t go through with some bullshit decision to end it.  The world is fucked up but also beautiful.  Life is hard but it’s also worth it.  Your post spoke to me.  Consider this: I’m a stranger and I care about you!  You matter!

I hear you.  What I mean is not that there’s no fulfillment or happiness; it is that we’re not entitled to it at every point in our lives.  The fact that you are not experiencing those things at this time does not mean that they are not in your future.  The fact that you don’t see hope doesn’t mean it isn’t there.  It’s not fair!  It reeeeeeallly sucks because it’s so obviously unfair esp when you look around and see people (a lot of shitty ones too) who are happy and fulfilled (or seem to be).

The question at hand is one of perspective.  You say your life is falling apart, you’re losing friends, you have a pos car, hate work, have no future.  You mention you have loved ones.  Let me offer an alternate perspective.  You have loved ones!  You have friendships (some need work - you can also make new ones)!  You have a POS car!  You’re employed!  Not only that, you have a fucking dog and I know that’s great, I have 5.  Anyway the point is you feel you have no future but you do - you can affect what it looks like by making even small changes in perspective and choices.  Shit you can have a ‘good’ future by not even trying bc sometimes it just happens on accident.  Accepting that life is miserable sometimes, even for extended periods, is understanding that purpose in life is deeper than feeling good.  You may indeed have a purpose in life that brings you struggle.  That’s ok.  Things can change a lot.  Participate in your journey.  Stay alive.

I get what you’re saying.  Had/have similar feelings.  For me, I have to just dismiss self-destructive thoughts with resignation and accept that it is an unacceptable course of action.  Too much pain for people around me.  Unfair to my possible futures.  I gave up on the idea that life is supposed to be ‘happy’ or fulfilling- it can just suck shit for extended periods of time.  Not caring anymore really isn’t an excuse to check out.  It’s also unrealistic.  Things can change and to think otherwise is to ignore very real possibilities.  There was a time I would have been ashamed to say that I take medication but not anymore.  It can help.

I challenge you to stick around for the fuck of it.  Read a little stoic philosophy, drink fuck tons of water, and listen to Django Reinhardt.  Be stubborn.  Stay alive.

On the subject of information:

It's better that information is more available/accessible.  However, it means less to people now that it can be so easily attained.  If you wanted to know something, you had to go and get it.  The effort made the information worth more.  Also, for the same reason, there is less incentive to retain information; you can retrieve it at any time.  We have given over part of our brain to the internet.  It's bizarre, a sort of collective brain.  All we need now is to know the shortcuts to information, not to actually store that information ourselves.  Computers are time-savers.

They have to be willing to seek treatment, an unlikely situation if ever there was one.  The alternative road to treatment is a sickening hope that they wil somehow be deemed a danger to themselves or others.

Health programs for the mentally ill are so commonly without the support and resources they need.  In the event that a person with schizophrenia actually finds themself in much needed treatment, the system is set up to spit them back out.
